name: Week 20 Legs — Steady State, Station-Grouped (Spotlight: Leg Press + Bulgarian)
description: Volume steady, station-grouped. **Warmup reminder:** bodyweight squat (depth check) → cross-leg lateral lean (QL/psoas) → hip circles → tibialis raise → cat-cow → internal core fist rotation → dead-bug core/QL primer → bodyweight lunge (QL check). Spotlights cycle forward to the leg press (deep-ROM refresh — it 'felt super open' W19 with the QL fresh) and the Bulgarian (stepped to double-50 DBs). The squat keeps the 45→70→80 ramp with the catcher bars set at your max-depth reference (W19: catcher at 14 = full bodyweight depth) — 80 held, depth the lever. Leg curl runs an explicit pyramid to a tested top (the W19 accidental 100 looked real on ~1 min rest). New this week: each lift is tagged 🔥 (near-failure/pyramid OK) or 🛑 (the cue/depth is the cap).

dayOverview.theme: Steady state, station-grouped. Spotlights cycle to the leg press (deep-ROM refresh — 'felt super open' W19) + the Bulgarian (double-50 DBs now). Squat keeps the 45→70→80 ramp + the catcher-14 max-depth reference; 80 held, depth the lever. Leg curl pyramids to a tested top (the W19 accidental 100 looked real). Dead-bug core primer stays in the warmup. Leg curl stays before incline RDL so the hamstring work doesn't stack.

spotlights.why: Cycles forward — W19 it 'felt super open' at 4 plates, a total contrast to W18's 'sweating like a wet dog' (the difference was a fresh, non-pre-fatigued QL). Spotlight drills the deep knees-to-chest ROM (the deep position trains the core/QL as much as the quads). The progression here is DEPTH + a near-failure last set at 4 plates — NOT more plates, because heavier plates shorten the deep ROM that's the whole point.

Cycles forward — W19 you stepped the DBs to double-50 ('feels fine, hard at end,' QL quiet). Spotlight drills the vertical-front-shin split stance + the drive through the front heel so double-50 stays clean and the QL stays quiet. Pigeon on the bench between sets (your W18 keeper) stays.

dayOverview.rotationPlan: W18 leg-press ROM + Bulgarian · W19 squat depth + leg curl · W20 leg press + Bulgarian (current) · W21 cycle forward — squat depth + calf / incline RDL refresh.
watchpoints: **🔥/🛑 intensity tags — decide before the set.** 🔥 near-failure / pyramid OK (safe machine/isolation): leg press (near-failure last set at 4 plates — depth is the load lever, not plates), calf raise, leg curl (pyramid the load to a tested top). 🛑 keep it shy, the cue/depth is the cap: squat (never grind a loaded squat — 'I'll fall on my face'), Bulgarian (QL/knee — form is the cap), incline RDL (hinge/lumbar — tempo is the lever). **Order:** form lever first (tempo/ROM), load second, near-failure/pyramid only on 🔥.

**Leg press spotlight — DEPTH is the lever, not plates.** Hold 4 plates; the deep knees-to-chest ROM is the work (it trains the core/QL). 🔥 It's a safe machine, so a near-failure LAST set at 4 plates is fair game if it feels open — but don't add plates to chase it, because heavier plates shorten the deep ROM and miss the point.

**Bulgarian spotlight — double-50 DBs (Smith @45 the QL-safe alternate).** W19 double-50 'feels fine, hard at end.' 🛑 form is the cap: front shin vertical, drive through the front heel, rear knee nearly to the floor. Pigeon on the bench between sets. If anything twitches, drop to bodyweight and finish.

**Leg curl pyramids to a tested top — the W19 100 looked real.** Run 70 primer → 80 → 90 → 100, judging the top by the FEEL (heels driving, no torso lift, slow eccentric), on NORMAL rest (the W19 100 was ~1 min rest = normal isolation rest, so it's a legit signal, not rest-flattered). 🔥 If 100 keeps the correct feel, it's yours; if it drifts, that's the honest top. Settings 5/m/0/-1 (verify before loading).

**Squat keeps the 45→70→80 ramp + the catcher-14 reference.** Set the catcher bars at your max bodyweight-bar depth (W19: 14) as a depth target + safety. 80 held — W19 was 'the most solid i ever felt, really stable' but not full depth; depth is the next unlock. 🛑 depth is the lever, never grind a loaded squat to failure. Stop adding working sets when the depth shortens.
**Dead-bug core/QL primer stays in the warmup.** W19 the leg press normalized with the QL fresh; keep waking the deep core before the leg press.
**Incline RDL holds 45, dead slow.** W19 did all 3 clean ('hard as always when done slowly'). 🛑 tempo (3s eccentric, 2s pause) is the lever, not the load.
**Station-grouped sequence:** warmup → squat → leg press → leg-press-calf-raise (SAME machine, stay there) → Bulgarian (bench station) → leg curl → incline RDL → cool-down. No backtracking.
**Keep leg curl BEFORE incline RDL** — reversed, the two hamstring lifts stack and smoke the second.

**QL/psoas watch** — cross-leg lateral lean in the warmup AND cool-down. QL's been clear (W19 legs 'felt easy,' no spasm). If anything talks in the warmup, modify the day; mid-session, drop a set + take stretch breaks.

sets.name: Warmup (incl. Cross-Leg Lateral Lean — QL/Psoas Release + Dead-Bug Core/QL Primer)

exercises.notes: Full depth, slow. Find where the hips are tight and breathe into it. Depth check before loading.

30s each side. Scissor one foot over the other, reach the same-side arm overhead, lean away from the back leg — the stretch runs down the side of the waist into the QL and lateral hip. Do this before loading the squat.
Big slow circles. Wake up the hip stabilizers.

Back to a wall, heels a step out, weight on the heels. Pull the toes UP toward the shins as high as they'll go, lower slow. Preps ankle dorsiflexion for squat depth + shin insurance for the run-in. ~30s, bodyweight.
Spine mobility — slow, full ROM each direction.

Standing, knees soft, torso hinged slightly forward. Tight fists with thumbs tucked, rotate the wrists internally and hold the tension. Quick posterior-chain + low-back opener before loading the squat.

**Core/QL primer.** On your back, arms up, knees over hips. Press the lower back FLAT into the floor and HOLD it there as you slowly extend the opposite arm + leg, then switch. The brace is the work — wakes the deep core before the leg press (W19: the leg press felt open with the QL primed + fresh).
Bodyweight. QL check — if anything talks here, modify the day. Also previews the Bulgarian pattern.

**The bottom half of the 45→70→80 ramp — set the catcher bars at your max-depth reference first (W19: 14 = full bodyweight-bar depth), as a depth target + safety.**
- **Set 1: 45/side x8** — drill max depth: sit all the way into the bottom, tap the catcher if you can, controlled reps, no bounce. W19 the 45 was deep, no 'hanging' moment.
- **Set 2: 70/side x8** — the intermediary ROM-builder. Same depth as the working sets, heavier so the bottom's honest. W19 the 70 was 'much deeper with more rest' but still a mid-range 'hanging moment' — breathe through it.
- **🛑 Move fast through these submaximal ramp sets** (short rest) — save the full rest for the 80 working sets.

**LOAD:** 80/side. Working sets off the ramp — run 80 for as many sets as the depth holds (W19 was 80x8 x2, 'the most solid i ever felt, really stable' but not full depth). **Depth is the lever, not reps or load.**
- Bar high on the upper traps, upper-back shelf squeezed
- **Brace like prepping for a punch** — deep belly breath at the top, HOLD through the descent, exhale on the drive up
- **Hips back AND down**, 'spread the floor' — screw the feet in, knees track over the toes
- **Sit into the bottom** — keep chasing depth toward the catcher; you find depth easier under load
- **Take the FULL rest here (2-3 min)** — W19 the deeper/more-solid sets came with more rest
- **🛑 Never grind a loaded squat to failure** — stop adding working sets when the depth shortens; a shallow grind isn't the work. Bank the deep, stable ones.

**Reflection:** does 80 hold the W19 stability AND start reaching closer to the catcher this week? Stability was last week's win; depth is the next. Deep + stable at 80 is the goal — if depth caps, that's the honest end.

sets.name: 🔆 Leg Press + Calf Raise Station (Same Machine — Leg Press Spotlight, Deep ROM) 🔥

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 4 plates/side. 4 sets of 12.

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — depth is the load lever, not plates:**
- **Full ROM — knees toward the chest.** The deep position trains the abs/QL/core as much as the quads — that's the intent
- **Foot position:** shoulder-width, mid-foot on the platform, slight toe-out
- **It feels harder cold** — the deep ROM opens once the hips are warm (W19 'felt super open'); don't judge the load on set 1
- **Actively press to keep the lower back from lifting off the pad** at the bottom; if the hips roll off, back off a hair
- **Press through the WHOLE foot; slow descent (3s), no bounce at the bottom**; don't lock out hard at the top
- **🔥 A near-failure LAST set at 4 plates is fair game** if it feels open — but DON'T add plates to chase it. Heavier plates shorten the deep ROM, and the deep ROM is the whole point. Depth first, then a hard last set at the SAME load.

**Reflection:** does the deep knees-to-chest ROM hold on all 4 sets (W19 'felt super open'), and does a near-failure last set stay deep — or does chasing the last few reps shorten the ROM? Deep-and-hard beats shallow-and-heavy.

**LOAD:** 4 plates/side. 3 sets of 15. Stay on the leg press — same machine, no walking off. 🔥
- **Balls of both feet on the BOTTOM EDGE of the platform, heels hanging off**
- **Full stretch at the bottom** — let the heels drop as far below the edge as they'll go
- **Drive to FULL plantarflexion at the top**
- **Tempo by feel** — own the stretch at the bottom and the squeeze at the top, no bouncing. 🔥 A hard last set is fine — it's a safe isolation. (3 sets, after the 4 leg-press sets — same station.)

sets.name: 🔆 Bulgarian Split Squat (Spotlight — Double-50 DBs; Smith @45 the Alternate; Pigeon Between Sets) 🛑

exercises.equipment: bench + DBs (regular default, double-50) — Smith machine if free (use smith-machine-bulgarian-split-squat)
exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** two 50lb DBs, one per hand (stepped up W19 — 'feels fine, hard at end'). 3 sets of 8-10 each leg. **Regular DB version is the default; the Smith machine @45 is the QL-safe alternate when it's free.**

**🔆 SPOTLIGHT — clean double-50, QL quiet:**
- **Rear foot up on the bench** behind you, laces down or toes tucked
- **Step out far enough that the front shin stays roughly VERTICAL at the bottom** — too short a stance = the knee crashes past the toes
- **Front knee tracks over the front foot** — not caving in
- **Lower until the rear knee nearly touches the floor** — controlled, no dropping
- **Drive up through the FRONT HEEL** — the front leg does the work, the rear leg is a kickstand
- **Torso TALL** — a slight forward lean is fine, no folding over; 2s descent, own the bottom
- **Pigeon on the bench between sets** — your W18 keeper, keeps the hip/QL loose under the load
- **🛑 Form is the cap — don't grind double-50 to failure.** At double-50 this is real load; if the QL/knee twitches, drop to bodyweight for the remaining sets and finish.

**Reflection:** does the front shin stay vertical and the drive stay in the front heel at double-50, or does the torso fold / the knee crash forward to move the weight? Clean double-50 is the win; a folding rep is the honest cap.

sets.name: Seated Leg Curl (Pyramid to a Tested Top — 5/m/0/-1, Before Incline RDL) 🔥

exercises.notes:
**LOAD — pyramid to a tested top:** 70 primer → 80 → 90 → 100. Slow tempo. **Settings: 5/m/0/-1** (verify before loading).

**🔥 The pyramid, judged by FEEL not the number:**
- **First set at 70 to groove the pattern** — 'primes my brain to do it correctly' (it'll feel easy; that's the point)
- **Then climb 80 → 90 → 100**, testing the top on NORMAL rest (~60-90s — the W19 accidental 100 was on ~1 min rest, which IS normal isolation rest, so it's a legit signal, not rest-flattered)
- **Ankles UNDER the pad** — the ankle bone is the contact point, NOT the mid-calf
- **Lap pad locked DOWN firmly** — a loose pad lets the torso lift and turns it into lower-back work
- **Curl the heels toward the glutes** — full ROM, full squeeze; **2s eccentric, 1s squeeze** — the slow eccentric is the whole stimulus
- **🔥 Judge the top by the correct FEEL** — heels driving, hamstring doing the work, torso anchored (no lifting forward). If 100 keeps that feel, it's yours; if it starts drifting (torso lifts, momentum creeps in), that's the honest top — drop back. The feel is the cap, not the stack.

**Reflection:** does 100 keep the 'correct' feel on normal rest, or does it drift into torso-lift and momentum? Correct feel at the top = the real number. This is a safe isolation — pyramiding up is exactly right here.

**LOAD:** 45lb plate. 3 sets of 15, dead slow with a 2s pause at the bottom (W19 did all 3 clean — 'hard as always when done slowly'). 🛑
- **Pad just below the hip crease** — NOT on the upper thigh, NOT on the stomach
- **Hip hinge** — a Romanian deadlift on the 45° bench, NOT a lumbar extension. Lower back NEUTRAL throughout
- **At the bottom:** the stretch is in the **hamstrings and glutes**, NOT the lower back. If the lumbar rounds, you're going too deep for current mobility
- **Drive up by squeezing the glutes and hamstrings**; at the top, stop at neutral — past neutral = lumbar load = QL irritation
- **Tempo: 3s eccentric, 2s pause at the bottom, 1s drive up.** 🛑 The slow eccentric is the entire lever — hold the 45lb plate, keep slowing the tempo; don't chase load or grind to failure on a hinge.

sets.name: Cool-Down — 5 Min Recovery Block (Hip/QL-Biased for Legs Day)

exercises.notes: 30s each side. Scissor the legs, reach overhead, lean away from the back leg — bookend the session with the same QL/psoas release as the warmup.
45s each side. Deep hip-flexor and glute release — the long hold lets the QL and psoas let go.
30s each side. Gentle twist for the QL — draw one knee across the body, opposite arm extended.
45s each side. Hip-rotator decompression.
60s slow breathing. Knees wide, arms extended forward. Parasympathetic shift.

sets.notes: 5-min recovery block, hip/QL-biased on legs day.

tips: **🔥/🛑 intensity tags this week.** 🔥 (near-failure/pyramid OK): leg press (near-failure last set at 4 plates — depth is the load lever, not plates), calf raise, leg curl (pyramid to a tested top). 🛑 (cue/depth/form is the cap): squat, Bulgarian, incline RDL. Form lever → load → near-failure/pyramid only on 🔥.
**Leg press spotlight — depth is the lever, not plates.** Hold 4 plates, deep knees-to-chest ROM; 🔥 a near-failure last set at 4 plates is fine, but don't add plates (that shortens the ROM).
**Bulgarian spotlight — double-50 DBs** (Smith @45 the alternate). Front shin vertical, drive through the front heel; pigeon between sets. 🛑 form is the cap.
**Leg curl pyramids — 70 → 80 → 90 → 100, judged by feel** (heels driving, no torso lift) on normal rest. The W19 100 looked real. 🔥
**Squat keeps the 45→70→80 ramp + the catcher-14 max-depth reference.** 80 held; depth is the next unlock after last week's stability win. 🛑
**Dead-bug core/QL primer stays in the warmup** — wakes the deep core before the leg press.
**Incline RDL holds 45, dead slow** — tempo (3s down, 2s pause) is the lever. 🛑
**Station-grouped:** warmup → squat → leg press → leg-press-calf-raise (same machine — stay there) → Bulgarian → leg curl → incline RDL → cool-down. No backtracking.
**Leg curl BEFORE incline RDL** — don't reverse them, or the hamstring work stacks.
**Cross-leg lateral lean in the warmup AND cool-down** — QL/psoas release. Take stretch breaks if anything's tight.
**Cool-down stays — 5-min block, hip/QL-biased on legs day.**
**Rest fast through the 45/70 ramp sets, full 2-3 min on the 80 working sets** — save the rest for where it counts. Rest: 2 min leg press, 90s calf raise + Bulgarian + leg curl + incline RDL.
formPhilosophy: Steady-state legs week. The leg press and Bulgarian get the spotlight — leg press around deep ROM (depth is the load lever, and a near-failure last set is the safe-machine outlet, not more plates), Bulgarian around clean double-50. The squat holds 80 with the ramp + the catcher-max-depth reference, depth the next unlock after W19's stability breakthrough. The leg curl leans into the user's pyramiding instinct on the one lift where it belongs — a safe isolation, load climbing to a top judged by the correct feel. The 🔥/🛑 tags make explicit which lifts take near-failure and which stay cue-capped. Form leads load — building decades, not weeks.
